name: AC Milan
fact: AC Milan was founded by Englishmen, which is why the club uses the English spelling 'Milan' rather than 'Milano'. They have won the European Cup seven times.

name: Ajax
fact: Ajax won three European Cups in a row from 1971 to 1973. Their academy has produced players such as Johan Cruyff, Dennis Bergkamp and Frenkie de Jong.

name: Al-Hilal
fact: Al-Hilal have won the AFC Champions League, Asia's top club competition, a record four times.

name: Al-Nassr
fact: Al-Nassr signed Cristiano Ronaldo in January 2023, a move that started a wave of big-name signings in the Saudi Pro League.

name: Argentinos Juniors
fact: Argentinos Juniors gave Diego Maradona his professional debut in 1976, ten days before his 16th birthday, and later named their stadium after him.

name: Arsenal
fact: Arsenal were founded by workers at the Royal Arsenal munitions factory in Woolwich, which is why they are called the Gunners. Their 'Invincibles' went the 2003–04 league season unbeaten.

name: Atlético Madrid
fact: Atlético's nickname, the Mattress Makers, comes from their red and white stripes, which looked like old mattress covers. Diego Simeone has coached them since 2011.

name: Barcelona
fact: Barcelona were founded in 1899 by the Swiss businessman Joan Gamper. The club's motto is 'Més que un club' (More than a club), and its La Masia academy produced Messi, Xavi and Iniesta.

name: Bayer Leverkusen
fact: Leverkusen were founded by workers at the Bayer pharmaceutical company. In 2023–24 they won their first Bundesliga title without losing a league game.

name: Bayern Munich
fact: Bayern Munich are Germany's most successful club, with six European Cups. Their Allianz Arena can light up its outside walls in different colours.

name: Benfica
fact: Benfica won back-to-back European Cups in 1961 and 1962. Before home games, a real eagle called Vitória flies around the Estádio da Luz.

name: Boca Juniors
fact: Boca Juniors were founded by Italian immigrants in the La Boca neighbourhood. Their blue and gold colours were inspired by the flag of a Swedish ship that sailed into the port.

name: Borussia Dortmund
fact: Dortmund's stadium has Europe's biggest standing terrace, the 'Yellow Wall', which holds about 25,000 fans. They won the Champions League in 1997.

name: Bryne
fact: Bryne, a small club near Stavanger on Norway's west coast, is where Erling Haaland started his career. His father Alf-Inge also played there.

name: Celtic
fact: Celtic were founded in 1887 to raise money for poor Irish immigrants in Glasgow's East End. In 1967 their 'Lisbon Lions', all born near Glasgow, became the first British team to win the European Cup.

name: Chelsea
fact: Chelsea were founded because the owner of Stamford Bridge wanted a team to play in his stadium. They won the Champions League in 2012 and 2021.

name: Corinthians
fact: Corinthians were named after Corinthian, an English amateur team that toured Brazil in 1910.

name: Dynamo Kyiv
fact: Dynamo Kyiv won the European Cup Winners' Cup twice, in 1975 and 1986, under the scientific coaching of Valeriy Lobanovskyi.

name: Everton
fact: Everton have spent more seasons in England's top division than any other club. In 2025 they moved from Goodison Park to a new stadium at Bramley-Moore Dock.

name: Feyenoord
fact: Feyenoord became the first Dutch club to win the European Cup, in 1970.

name: Flamengo
fact: Flamengo started as a rowing club in 1895 and added football in 1911. They are often called the best-supported club in Brazil.

name: Galatasaray
fact: Galatasaray were founded by students at the Galatasaray High School in Istanbul. In 2000 they became the first Turkish club to win a European trophy, the UEFA Cup.

name: Hamburger SV
fact: Hamburger SV won the European Cup in 1983. Their stadium used to have a clock counting how long they had been in the Bundesliga, until they were relegated for the first time in 2018.

name: Budapest Honvéd
fact: Honvéd, formerly called Kispest, provided most of the 'Mighty Magyars' team that reached the 1954 World Cup final, including Ferenc Puskás.

name: Independiente del Valle
fact: Independiente del Valle, from near Quito, are famous for their academy and won the Copa Sudamericana in 2019 and 2022.

name: Inter Miami
fact: Inter Miami were founded by David Beckham and his partners. Lionel Messi led them to their first trophy, the 2023 Leagues Cup, weeks after he arrived.

name: Inter Milan
fact: Inter was founded in 1908 by members who left AC Milan because they wanted to sign foreign players, hence the name 'Internazionale'. Both clubs share the San Siro.

name: Juventus
fact: Juventus were founded by students in Turin. Their black-and-white stripes came from Notts County in England, after a shipment of pink shirts kept fading.

name: LA Galaxy
fact: LA Galaxy have won MLS Cup a record six times. David Beckham's move there in 2007 put Major League Soccer in the global spotlight.

name: Lazio
fact: Lazio play in sky blue and white, the colours of Greece, as a tribute to the home of the Olympic Games. They share the Stadio Olimpico with city rivals Roma.

name: Le Havre
fact: Le Havre is the oldest football club in France, founded in 1872.

name: Leicester City
fact: Leicester won the 2015–16 Premier League after starting the season as 5000-to-1 outsiders, one of the biggest shocks in sport.

name: Liverpool
fact: Liverpool have won six European Cups, more than any other English club. Fans sing 'You'll Never Walk Alone' before every home game at Anfield.

name: Malmö FF
fact: Malmö FF reached the European Cup final in 1979, the only Swedish club to do so.

name: Manchester City
fact: Manchester City began life as St. Mark's (West Gorton), a church team. In 2023 they won the treble of Premier League, FA Cup and Champions League.

name: Manchester United
fact: Manchester United started as Newton Heath, a railway workers' team. They have won 20 English league titles, and Old Trafford is nicknamed the 'Theatre of Dreams'.

name: Marseille
fact: Marseille became the first French club to win the Champions League, in 1993.

name: Molde
fact: Molde, on Norway's west coast, won the Norwegian league three times under Ole Gunnar Solskjær, and gave Erling Haaland his breakthrough.

name: Nacional
fact: Nacional were founded in 1899 as the first club in Uruguay created by local people rather than British immigrants.

name: Napoli
fact: Napoli won their first two Serie A titles with Diego Maradona, in 1987 and 1990, and renamed their stadium after him in 2020.

name: New York Cosmos
fact: The New York Cosmos signed Pelé in 1975 and Franz Beckenbauer in 1977, drawing huge crowds to football in the United States.

name: Newell's Old Boys
fact: Newell's Old Boys in Rosario is the club where Lionel Messi played as a boy before moving to Barcelona.

name: Nottingham Forest
fact: Nottingham Forest won the European Cup in 1979 and 1980, just a few years after being promoted from the second division under Brian Clough.

name: Paris Saint-Germain
fact: PSG were founded only in 1970. In 2025 they won their first Champions League, beating Inter 5–0 in the biggest winning margin in a final.

name: Porto
fact: Porto won the Champions League in 2004 under José Mourinho, and the European Cup in 1987.

name: PSV Eindhoven
fact: PSV were founded for workers of the electronics company Philips, which is what the 'P' stands for. They won the European Cup in 1988.

name: Red Bull Salzburg
fact: Red Bull Salzburg's scouting network helped launch Erling Haaland, Sadio Mané and Dominik Szoboszlai on their way to Europe's biggest clubs.

name: Real Madrid
fact: Real Madrid have won the European Cup a record 15 times, including the first five editions from 1956 to 1960. 'Real' means royal: King Alfonso XIII gave the club the title in 1920.

name: Santos
fact: Pelé spent almost his whole career at Santos, and the club also launched Neymar. During a 1969 tour, a ceasefire was reportedly called in Nigeria's civil war so people could watch Pelé play.

name: Sevilla
fact: Sevilla have won the UEFA Cup and Europa League a record seven times.

name: Southampton
fact: Southampton's academy has produced Gareth Bale, Theo Walcott and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain. The club started as a church team, which is why they are called the Saints.

name: Sporting CP
fact: Sporting's academy produced both Cristiano Ronaldo and Luís Figo, two Ballon d'Or winners.

name: Tottenham Hotspur
fact: Tottenham's name comes from Harry Hotspur, a medieval nobleman whose family owned land in the area. In 1961 they became the first club in the 20th century to win the English league and FA Cup double.

name: Villarreal
fact: Villarreal come from a town of about 50,000 people, yet won the Europa League in 2021. Their nickname, the Yellow Submarine, comes from the Beatles song.
